dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ) and they covered themselves with them, as though they sought that their garments should cover them, or that [the garments] should cover them, so that they would not see him, out of aversion to looking at one who counsels them about the religion of Allah.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ) Inna and its noun, and the clause أرسلنا is its khabar (predicate); نوحا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and إلى قومه is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا. (أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) An may be maṣdariyya, so together with what it governs it is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to أرسلنا; the meaning is: We sent him by saying to him "Warn". It may also be explicative, because sending contains the meaning of saying. أنذر is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; قومك is the direct object; من قبل is attached to أنذر. An and what falls in its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the genitive by construct; يأتيهم is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the hāʾ is the direct object; عذاب is the agent and أليم an adjective (naʿt). (قالَ يا قَوْمِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) قال is a past verb and its agent is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; يا is a vocative particle and قوم is the one addressed (munādā), in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the first person; the discussion of the munādā in construct with the first-person yāʾ has preceded. Inna and its noun; لكم is attached to نذير; نذير is the khabar and مبين an adjective. (أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ) An is maṣdariyya or explicative; the discussion of it has just preceded. اعبدوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; الله is the direct object; اتقوه and أطيعون are conjoined to اعبدوا. The first-person yāʾ was dropped to match the verse-endings, i.e. وأطيعوني. (يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى) يغفر is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer of the command; لكم is attached to يغفر; من ذنوبكم is in the position of the accusative as the object of يغفر, because min is partitive, i.e. some of your sins, since faith wipes out the sins before it, not those after it. It is said it is for the beginning of the extent, and it is said it is redundant (zāʾida); this is the school of al-Akhfash, because he permits its redundancy in affirmative and other contexts, whereas the Basrans and most of the Kufans stipulate for its redundancy that it be preceded by a negation, a prohibition or a question, and that it come before an indefinite noun. يؤخركم is conjoined to يغفر and the kāf is the direct object; إلى أجل is attached to يؤخركم and مسمى is an adjective of أجل. We shall present an interesting discussion about this postponement of the punishment in the section on benefits. (إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ إِذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) The clause gives the reason for what preceded. Inna and its noun; إذا is an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive, attached to its apodosis; the clause جاء is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; the clause لا يؤخر has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition that does not cause the jussive. Law is conditional; كنتم is kāna and its noun, and the clause تعلمون is its khabar. The apodosis of law is omitted, just as the object of تعلمون is omitted, i.e. if you knew that, you would believe. (قالَ: رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلًا وَنَهاراً) ربّ is a munādā in construct with the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the vocative particle is omitted. Inna and its noun, and the clause دعوت is its khabar; قومي is the direct object; ليلا and نهارا are two adverbs attached to دعوت. The clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعائِي إِلَّا فِراراً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; lam is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and the jussive; يزدهم is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lam, and the hāʾ is the first direct object; دعائي is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction and فرارا is the second direct object; the exception is emptied (mufarragh). (وَإِنِّي كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ فِي آذانِهِمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; inna and its noun; كلما is an adverb attached to جعلوا, with mā being maṣdariyya or an indefinite noun. دعوتهم is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the lām is causal, and تغفر is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, optionally implied after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to دعوتهم. The clause جعلوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, namely كلما. أصابعهم is the first object of جعلوا and في آذانهم is in the place of the second object. (وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا اسْتِكْباراً) استغشوا is conjoined to جعلوا and ثيابهم is the direct object; أصرّوا and استكبروا are also conjoined; استكبارا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهاراً) ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; inna and its noun, and the clause دعوتهم is its khabar; جهارا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, being a maṣdar from the meaning [of the verb], because calling may be open or otherwise, so it is of the type رجع القهقرى ("he went back backwards") and قعد القرفصاء ("he sat squatting"). It may also be a maṣdar in place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. openly and in an open manner, and making it the maṣdar itself is hyperbole. (ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَعْلَنْتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْراراً) conjoined to what preceded; إسرارا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «واستغشوا ثيابهم» there is a metonymy (kināya) for the extremity of their turning away from what he called them to: they are like someone who has blocked his hearing and covered his sight so as not to hear and see. One says, "So-and-so put on the garments of enmity". It is also said that the expression is literal, and the meaning of استغشوا ثيابهم is that they covered their faces with them so as not to see me, or put their garments over their heads so as not to hear my speech; on this view, covering with the garments is an addition to blocking the ears.
In the delay [expressed by thumma] and the repetition of the call there is clarification and emphasis. In this connection we quote the wording of al-Zamakhsharī because of its excellence. He said: «If you say: He mentioned that he called them by night and by day, then called them openly, then called them in secret and in public; so these must be three different calls for the conjunction to be valid — I say: He, upon him be blessing and peace, did as one who commands the right and forbids the wrong does, beginning with the lightest and rising to the more severe and then the more severe still. He began with counselling in secret; when they did not accept, he followed with openness as the second step; when that had no effect, he made the third step combining secrecy and openness. The meaning of thumma is to indicate the remoteness of the states from one another, because openness is harsher than secrecy, and combining the two matters is harsher than doing one of them alone». This is splendid speech whose depth few can fathom: it is known from His words ثم إني دعوتهم جهارا that the preceding call was in secret, so the thumma conveyed the disparity between openness and the preceding secrecy, and the second thumma conveyed that combining the two is harsher than each of them alone.

* Benefits:
Now, we promised you to present an enjoyable discussion that arose among the great exegetes about His words ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: How did He say ويؤخركم while informing that the postponement of the term is impossible, and is this anything but a contradiction? I say: Allah decreed, for example, that if the people of Noah believed He would let them live a thousand years, and if they remained in their disbelief He would destroy them at the end of nine hundred. So it was said to them: Believe, and He will postpone you to a named term, i.e. to a time that Allah has named and set as a limit which you reach and do not exceed, and that is the longer time, the completion of the thousand. Then He informed that when that term, the limit, comes, it is not postponed as this [other] time is postponed, and you would have no recourse; so hasten in the times of respite and postponement».
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى is among what the Muʿtazila clung to in their saying that a person has two terms. They said: If it were one fixed term, then neither postponement would be valid if the limit had been reached, nor hastening [Translator's note: the source has «المعالجة», apparently for «المعاجلة», "hastening"] if it had not been reached». He said: «They have no hold in the verse, because the meaning is that Noah, upon him be peace, did not know whether they were among those who would be postponed or those who would be hastened [to punishment], nor did he say to them that you will be postponed beyond a term that has arrived for you. Rather, it was preordained from eternity that they were either among those for whom faith and postponement were decreed, or among those for whom disbelief and hastening were decreed. Then this meaning was strengthened and made apparent by His words: إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر».
Al-Suyūṭī cleared away the obscurity that encroached on this expression by saying in his enjoyable commentary: «and He will postpone you without punishment», i.e. in this world; so it does not conflict with His words إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر, because what is negated there as being postponed is the term itself, so there is no conflict between these two places.
The wording of al-Karkhī in his gloss on the Jalālayn: «His words "and He will postpone you without punishment" answer [the question]: how did He say ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى in addressing the people of Noah? For if what is meant is postponing them beyond the term decreed from eternity, that is impossible because of His words, the Exalted: ولن يؤخّر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها; or [if it is] postponing them until the coming of their decreed term, as with others, whether they believe or not, [then it has no point]. [Translator's note: the bracketed completion is added for clarity; the source sentence is elliptical.] Its clarification is that its meaning is: He will postpone the punishment from you until the end of your terms, on the supposition of faith, so He will not punish you in this world if a sin occurs from you, as He punished other disbelieving nations in it».

dervis-irab:10-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مِدْراراً) pouring abundantly; masculine and feminine are the same in it, and this sameness holds regularly in the pattern mifʿāl, a form of intensification.
(أَطْواراً) plural of ṭawr, which is the state and the time (tāra). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «al-ṭawr, with fatḥa, is a time: "he did that ṭawran after ṭawr", i.e. time after time. Al-ṭawr is also the state and the form; the plural is aṭwār, like thawb and athwāb. "He overstepped his ṭawr", i.e. the state befitting him».
(فِجاجاً) wide; plural of fajj, which is the wide road; it is said it is the passage between two mountains.

* I'rab:
(فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قلت is a verb and its agent; استغفروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ربكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Inna and its noun, and the clause كان is its khabar (predicate); the noun of kāna is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa", and غفارا is its khabar. The clause استغفروا is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause إنه كان غفارا has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for seeking forgiveness. In al-Shihāb: «What is meant by seeking forgiveness is not merely saying "I seek Allah's forgiveness", but turning back from sins and purifying tongues and hearts». (يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً) يرسل is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer of the command; the agent is latent, referring to Allah the Exalted; السماء is the direct object; عليكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرسل; مدرارا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السماء. (وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهاراً) يمددكم is conjoined to يرسل and the kāf is the direct object; بأموال is attached to يمددكم and بنين is conjoined to أموال; يجعل is an imperfect verb in the jussive, conjoined to يمددكم; لكم is in the place of the second object and جنات is the direct object; ويجعل لكم أنهارا is conjoined to the previous clause. What is meant by جنات is the orchards of this world. (ما لَكُمْ لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقاراً) ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لكم is the khabar; lā is negative and ترجون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; the clause لا ترجون is a ḥāl from the kāf in لكم. لله is a ḥāl, because the lām is for clarification; had it come later it would have been an adjective of الوقار. وقارا is the direct object of ترجون, i.e. reverence and veneration. Further clarification of this expression will come in the section on benefits. (وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْواراً) The wāw is circumstantial; qad is a particle of realisation; خلقكم is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of ترجون. أطوارا is a ḥāl interpreted as a derived word, i.e. passing from state to state. (أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقاً) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; lam is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and the jussive; تروا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. The seeing is cognitive, i.e. have you not taken heed and reflected? كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, governed by خلق. خلق الله is a past verb and its agent, and the clause stands in place of the two objects of تروا, which is suspended from governing by the interrogative. سبع سموات is the direct object, and طباقا is an adjective of سبع, i.e. one above another; or it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "they were made in layers (ṭubbiqat ṭibāqan)", so it would be the maṣdar of طابقت مطابقة وطباقا. That was mentioned in Sūrat al-Mulk. (وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجاً) The wāw is a conjunction; جعل القمر is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; فيهن is a ḥāl and نورا is the second direct object; وجعل الشمس سراجا is conjoined to the previous clause. (وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أنبتكم is the khabar; من الأرض is attached to أنبتكم; نباتا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). It may be a maṣdar of أنبت with the additional letters dropped, and this is called a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); or it may be the maṣdar of an implied نبتم, i.e. "and you grew a growing", so it is accusative by the implied reflexive verb (al-muṭāwiʿ). The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «The meaning is: He caused you to grow and you grew a growing; or it is accusative by أنبتكم because it contains the meaning of نبتم». (ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيها وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْراجاً) conjoined to what preceded. (وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِساطاً) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause جعل is the khabar; لكم is a ḥāl; الأرض is the first direct object and بساطا the second direct object. (لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنْها سُبُلًا فِجاجاً) The lām is the lām of cause; تسلكوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the causal lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to جعل. منها is a ḥāl from سبلا, i.e. being from the earth; had it come later it would have been an adjective of it. سبلا is the direct object and فجاجا an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا» there is a synecdoche-type metaphor (majāz mursal) whose relation is that of place: by السماء He meant the rain, because rain comes down from it. A poet said:
إذا نزل السماء بأرض قوم ... رعيناه وإن كانوا غضابا
(When the sky [i.e. rain] comes down on a people's land, we graze it, even if they are angry.)
What is meant by the verse is describing their courage: if they dare to graze the plants of angry people, they are all the more likely to dare against others. In the verse there is also istikhdām (using a word in one sense and its pronoun in another): he used السماء and returned the pronoun to it with the meaning of plants, because it is their cause.
2- In His words «والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because He likened them to plants: He borrowed "causing to grow" for "bringing into being", as one says "May Allah plant you for good". This metaphor had a benefit, because it indicated origination in time: if they are plants, they are inevitably originated, as plants are originated. Because of this the Ḥashwiyya were called "al-Nābitiyya" and "al-Nawābit" (the sprouts), on account of the newness of their school in Islam.

* Benefits:
The sayings of the exegetes differed concerning His words «ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا». We present here extracts from their sayings and then follow them with what clears up their obscurity. Al-rajāʾ means hope and fear. Abū ʿUbayda said: «لا ترجون: you do not fear». They said: al-waqār means greatness and authority, so the speech is a threat and an intimidation. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «The meaning is: what is the matter with you that you are not in a state in which you hope for Allah's honouring you in the abode of reward? لله clarifies the one who is honoured; had it come later it would have been a complement (ṣila) of الوقار … Or: you do not fear Allah's forbearance and His refraining from hastening the punishment, so that you might believe. It is said: what is the matter with you that you do not fear the greatness of Allah? And from Ibn ʿAbbās: you do not fear an outcome from Allah, because the outcome is the state in which matters settle and reward and punishment become fixed, from وقر when it became fixed and settled». The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «It is said: what is the matter with you that you do not make your hope in Allah and your encounter with Him a sedateness (waqār)? On this view it would be from them, as though He says: deliberation on your part and steadiness in reflection, because thought is a likely place of levity, rashness and obstinacy». Quṭrub said: This is a Ḥijāzī dialect; Hudhayl, Khuzāʿa and Muḍar say لم أرجُ meaning "I did not care".
The wording of Abū al-Suʿūd: «ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا is a disapproval of their having any reason at all for their not believing in a greatness for Allah the Exalted, on the basis that al-rajāʾ means belief. لا ترجون is a ḥāl from the pronoun of those addressed, and what governs it is the meaning of being settled in لكم. لله is attached to an implied element that occurs as a ḥāl from وقارا; had it come later it would have been an adjective of it. That is: what reason has come to you, while you do not believe in a greatness for Allah the Exalted that requires venerating Him by believing in Him and obeying Him, وقد خلقكم أطوارا, i.e. while you are in a state wholly at odds with what you are doing, namely that you know that He, the Exalted, created you at one stage as elements, then as nourishment, then as humours, then as drops of fluid, then as clinging clots, then as lumps of flesh, then as bones and flesh, then brought you into being as another creation. For falling short in revering one whose affairs are such, in overpowering might and perfect beneficence, while knowing them, is something that hardly issues from a rational being».
What we derive from all this is that the people went to extremes in despising him, upon him be peace, mocking him and making jokes about him; so Allah commanded them to adhere earnestly to revering and respecting him and to turn away from this unbecoming treatment. That is: if you revere Noah and abandon belittling him and making jokes about him, that will be obedience to Allah, drawing near to Him and compliance with His commands; so what is the matter with you that you do not seize this opportunity and attain the pleasure of Allah by revering and respecting him?

dervis-irab:21-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كُبَّاراً) with ḍamma on the kāf and doubling of the bāʾ; it is a form of intensification more intense than كُبار, with ḍamma and without doubling. (ود، سواع، يَغُوثَ، يَعُوقَ، نسر) names of idols they used to worship.
(دَيَّاراً) Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is one of the nouns used in general negation. One says ما بالدار ديّار and ديّور, like قيّام and قيّوم. It is a fayʿāl from al-dawr or from al-dār, and its origin is دَيْوار, and what was done to the origin of سيّد and ميّت was done to it; had it been a faʿʿāl, it would have been دوّار». The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «ديّارا is one of the words of generality used in negation and what resembles it. Its pattern is fayʿāl; its origin is دَيْوار: the yāʾ and the wāw came together, the first of them having a sukūn, so they were assimilated». In al-Qāmūs: «ما به داريّ, ديّار, دوريّ and ديّور: [there is not in it] anyone».
(تَباراً) destruction.

* I'rab:
(قالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي) قال نوح is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); رب is the one addressed (munādā), in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the first person; inna and its noun, and the clause عصوني is its khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَاتَّبَعُوا مَنْ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ مالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ إِلَّا خَساراً) اتبعوا is conjoined to عصوني; من is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); lam is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and the jussive; يزده is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is the direct object; ماله is the agent and ولده is conjoined to ماله; إلا is a particle of restriction and خسارا is the second direct object of يزده. (وَمَكَرُوا مَكْراً كُبَّاراً) The wāw is a conjunction; مكروا is a past verb and its agent; مكرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and كبارا is an adjective (naʿt) of مكرا, i.e. exceedingly great. (وَقالُوا لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلا سُواعاً وَلا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْراً) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a past verb and its agent; lā is prohibitive and تذرن is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw [of the agent] is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; آلهتكم is the direct object. ولا تذرن is conjoined to the first لا تذرن, and ودّا and what is conjoined to it are the object of تذرن. يغوث and يعوق are diptotes because of being proper names together with the verbal pattern, if they are Arabic, or being proper names together with foreignness, if they are foreign. It was read ولا يغوثا ويعوقا, fully declined, for two reasons: first, that they were declined for harmony, since before them come two declined nouns and after them a declined noun; second, that it follows the dialect of those who decline the diptote absolutely, a dialect reported by al-Kisāʾī. (وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلالًا) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause قد أضلوا is the object of an omitted saying, conjoined to the preceding قال, i.e. he said: "they have disobeyed me", and he said: "they have led astray". أضلوا is a verb and its agent and كثيرا is the direct object. The wāw conjoins to the omitted saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: To what is His word ولا تزد الظالمين conjoined? I say: To his word رب إنهم عصوني, by way of relating the speech of Noah, upon him be peace, after قال and after the wāw that stands in for it. Its meaning is: he said "My Lord, they have disobeyed me" and he said "Do not increase the wrongdoers except in error", i.e. he said these two sayings, and they are in the position of the accusative because they are the two objects of قال». Lā is prohibitive and تزد is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā; الظالمين is an object; إلا is a particle of restriction and ضلالا is the direct object. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «ولا تزد is conjoined to قد أضلوا because it is related by an implied قال; harmony is not stipulated in conjoined clauses; rather, a statement may be conjoined to a request and vice versa, contrary to those who stipulated it». The wording of al-Shihāb al-Khafājī: «That is, لا تزد is a second saying of Noah, upon him be peace. Allah conjoined one of his two sayings to the other, and the wāw in it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, not from the speech of Noah, because that would entail conjoining a performative (inshāʾ) to a statement (ikhbār). So Allah related one of his two sayings by heading it with the word قال, and related his other saying by conjoining it to his first saying with the wāw that stands in for the word قال». (مِمَّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا ناراً) Min is a preposition and mā is redundant (zāʾida); خطيئاتهم is genitive (majrūr) by causal min, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أغرقوا; أغرقوا is a past passive verb. فأدخلوا is conjoined to أغرقوا; their entering the Fire was made to follow immediately upon their drowning in view of its nearness, and because it will inevitably be, so it is as though it had already been. نارا is the second direct object, by extension of usage. (فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْصاراً) also a conjoining with immediate succession; lam is a particle of negation, conversion and the jussive; يجدوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lam; لهم is in the place of the second object of يجدوا; من دون الله is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and أنصارا is the first object of يجدوا. (وَقالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ دَيَّاراً) The wāw is a conjunction; قال نوح is a past verb and its agent; رب is a munādā from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and it is in construct with the omitted first-person yāʾ. Lā is prohibitive and تذر is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā; على الأرض is attached to تذر; من الكافرين is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of ديارا; ديارا is the object of تذر. (إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فاجِراً كَفَّاراً) Inna and its noun, and the clause gives the reason for Noah's request, upon him be peace. If it is asked: How did he know that their children would be like them? It is answered that he remained among them a thousand years less fifty, so he fathomed their inner selves and sounded their depths: a man among them would go off with his son and say to him:
"Beware of this man, for he is a liar, and my father warned me against him"; then the old would die and the young would grow up upon what his father had taught and instilled in him before. In is conditional; تذرهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and the hāʾ is the direct object; يضلوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of إنك. عبادك is the direct object. The wāw is a conjunction, lā is negative, and يلدوا is an imperfect verb conjoined to يضلوا, and the wāw is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction, فاجرا is the object of يضلوا [Translator's note: so in the source; the governing verb of فاجرا is evidently يلدوا], and كفارا is an adjective. (رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوالِدَيَّ وَلِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِناً وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ) رب is a munādā in construct; its like has preceded. اغفر is a verb of supplication; لي is attached to اغفر; لوالدي is conjoined to لي and لمن is also conjoined; the clause دخل بيتي is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and مؤمنا is a ḥāl; للمؤمنين والمؤمنات is also conjoined. (وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَباراً) The wāw is a conjunction; lā is prohibitive in supplication; تزد is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā; الظالمين is the first direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction and تبارا is the second direct object; the exception is emptied (mufarragh). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «تبر يتبر, of the patterns of قتل and تعب, when he perished; it becomes transitive by doubling, so one says تبّره, and the noun is التبار. The faʿāl pattern, with fatḥa, often comes from faʿʿala, as in كلّم كلاما, سلّم سلاما and ودّع وداعا».

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ولا يلدوا إلا فاجرا كفّارا» there is a synecdoche-type metaphor (majāz mursal) whose relation is what [the thing] will become, because they will not be wicked at the time of birth but, in any case, a long time after it.
